title: The light chooses its vessel: the Names of Adam Kadmon, the three governors, and the tikunim
overview:
The chapter gives the *nimshal* of the soul in the body. The light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, as it comes from *Adam Kadmon*, is like the soul's intellect before the brain: one with its source, and its revelation only a color, like the apple's. Yet once G-d chooses a color it becomes essential, as wanting to help this person is bound to being nice. So in *Adam Kadmon* G-d chose to be wise, to create and to rule, though to Him all-knowing is no more a praise than "all-stupid", and the lights of the *sefiros* are still *b'li ma*.

These choices are the Names: *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*. Before *Atzilus* they are the source of the lights; after it, as the brain, the heart and the liver, they are the vessels made from the light's thickening, as a chair takes the shape of its sitter. So one should pray to the light, and the vessel follows. The vessels are also *tikunim*, like glasses for the eye or a uniform: they let the light come down, and let us see G-d without being burned.

terms.gloss: sefiros without a what: the lights of Atzilus, not yet defined, infinite compared to the vessels
the will for the will: the essential will connected to a particular will, which makes the particular essential
the names of the Emanator: the four Names of Adam Kadmon, the way G-d chose to reveal Himself
thickening: the end of the light, the part of it that relates to physical things, of which the vessel is made
three levels of the soul: the neshama, intellect, in the brain; the ruach, emotion, in the heart; and the nefesh, life, in the liver
the somethingness of the light: its ego, its tangibleness, when it seems to be a distinct entity
intending: directing the mind in prayer, to the light and not to the vessel
faith: trusting that G-d will make everything come out for the best, without worrying about the vessel
trust: an opposite avoda, which focuses on the vessel (to be explained later)
garments or fixers: vessels as they transform the light into a particular expression that reaches a lower level, like glasses for the eye
the campaigns, given as an example of why G-d would want to give a person what he asks for

sections.title: The nimshal: the light of chachma before the vessel is like the soul's intellect before the brain
sections.summary: The light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, as it comes from *Adam Kadmon*, is like the soul's power of intellect before it goes into the brain: one with its source, like the fire inside the coal. What comes out is only like the color of an apple, a separate sign of the essence.

phrases.he: (כח) והנמשל מדוגמא זו
phrases.en: The *nimshal* from this comparison of the way the soul goes into the body

phrases.he: הוא בבחינת ג' כלים דמוחא ולבא כו'

blocks.text: The *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) of the soul entering the body. *Dugma* (a likeness) means an example, closer than an analogy: the way your soul goes into your body is *mamash* (literally) the same thing, only smaller. The *nimshal* is the three main vessels of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation), **the brain, the heart and the liver**, **at least in general, that's the general idea**.

phrases.he: דאור החכמה דאצילות מצד אצילותה מעצמות אור המאציל,
phrases.en: the light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, the way that it's originally emanated from the *Atzmus* of the light of the *ma'atzil*

phrases.he: הרי זה כאור השכל הרוחני עצמו
phrases.en: like the spiritual power of *sechel*

phrases.he: שנמשך מעצם כח החכמה שבבחינת עצמות הנפש
שמתאחד הוא עדיין במקור חוצבו ממש
phrases.en: that there it's totally one with its source

blocks.text: The light of *chachma* (wisdom) of *Atzilus*, as it first comes from the *Atzmus* (G-d's essence) of the *ma'atzil* (the one who emanates; generally *Adam Kadmon*), is only a *gilui* (revelation) of G-d. Everything before *Atzilus*, down to its lights, is like the soul before it enters the body. So *chachma* coming out of *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man; the first world) is like the soul's *sechel* (intellect) before it reaches the brain: **the spiritual power of sechel**, from the essence of *chachma* in the essence of the soul.

There it is **totally one with its source**. Before it comes into the body it is just you; you do not see the *sechel* as a separate power that you have. Only in the body and the brain is it revealed as its own thing, intellect.

phrases.he: כשלהבת כו'
או גם כגלוי הרצון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: or like the *ratzon*

phrases.he: מעצם הרצון דבחינת אדם קדמון

blocks.title: The flame and the coal
blocks.text: The real existence of the *sechel* is only a revealing of you. What we see of it is like the flame outside the coal, its *gilui*; its essence is hidden, like the fire burning inside the coal. So a person has a power of intellect, a certain genius, there in his soul inherently, and what we see is only its revelation, seemingly separate from the soul, as it reflects through the body.

**Or like the ratzon**: the essential *ratzon* (will) of *Adam Kadmon*, as with the *ratzon l'ratzon* (the will for the will). The inner will, before it comes out, is to express yourself: since you essentially have *sechel*, you want to reveal yourself by being wise. A particular desire, like helping a lady across the street, only reflects the inner desire to be kind; the circumstances show that this is kind, so you have a *ratzon l'ratzon* for it. What you essentially want is not its *pratim* (details).

phrases.he: הגם שזהו כמו מראה וגוון בלבד,
phrases.en: even though this relationship is only like an appearance and a color

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב למעלה בענין קורא הדורות מראש
phrases.en: like explained before about the calling it *meirosh*, up in the beginning

phrases.he: שזהו עשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: which is the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שיצאו מהעלם דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: which go out from the hidden of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שהוא גילוי רצון בדבר נבדל כו'
בסוף אות הי"ט)
phrases.en: explained at the end of *os* 19

blocks.text: **Even though this relationship is only like an appearance and a color**: the revelation that comes out is a totally separate, limited thing, with no real connection to the *etzem* (essence).

blocks.title: The color of an apple
blocks.text:
The color of an apple tells you whether it is ripe: green is not ripe, at least for red apples; red is ripe. A white inside tells you it is sweet; brownish means it is not. But the colors are not connected to the sweetness. They only reveal it; the sweetness is there regardless of the color you see.

So too a person is smart before he shows it by solving some problem. The potential is in his soul; what you see is just an external way of expressing it.

As explained above on *kore hadoros meirosh* (He calls the generations from the beginning), **which is the ten sefiros of Atzilus** coming out of the hidden of *Adam Kadmon*: a revelation of will in a separate thing, as at the end of section 19.

sections.title: Still sefiros b'li ma: once G-d chooses the color, it becomes essential
sections.summary: The lights of *Atzilus* are still undefined, *b'li ma*, because a color that is only a sign becomes bound to the taste, as wanting to help this person becomes bound to being a nice person. In *Adam Kadmon* G-d chose to be wise, a creator and a master, and so these became G-dly attributes, in themselves no more a praise than "all-stupid".

phrases.he: עם כל זה
phrases.en: nevertheless

phrases.he: נקרא עשר ספירות בלי מ''ה, בלי מהות עדיין
phrases.en: the lights are still called the ten *sefiros* without *ma*, *b'li ma*: they're not defined

blocks.text: **Nevertheless**, the lights are still called the ten *sefiros b'li ma* (*sefiros* without a what): **they're not defined**, even the *gilui* of them, when it comes out.

phrases.he: כי כמו שהגוון הוא גם כן עצמי,
phrases.en: but in a way this is also essential

phrases.he: שאי אפשר להיות גוון היפוכו לדבר בעצם
phrases.en: It's impossible to have an opposite color for it

phrases.he: כגוון התפוח בלובן, להורות על עצם טעם המתיקות שבו
phrases.en: like the whiteness of an apple on the inside, which shows the sweetness of it.

blocks.text: The lights of *Atzilus* are only the *gilui* of *Adam Kadmon*, like the will to help the old lady across the street, or the apple's color: in a way already separate from the essence, **but in a way this is also essential**. **It's impossible to have an opposite color for it**. That this color means sweetness is circumstantial, but now the two are bound together: with that taste the apple has to be this color, **like the whiteness of an apple on the inside, which shows the sweetness of it**.

phrases.he: וכן אור השכל ורצון מטה כלפי חסד,
phrases.en: and similarly if a person has this desire or this direction in his intellect and his desire that leans towards kindness

phrases.he: גם שהוא בענין נבדל,
phrases.en: even though this is in a very specific, detailed thing

phrases.he: מאחר שהוא מורה על העצם כו'

blocks.text: **And similarly**, a person with a direction in his intellect and desire **that leans towards kindness** in a particular situation, who wants to do a nice thing and looks at it with a nice eye, shows that he is a nice person. **Even though this is in a very specific, detailed thing**, once it is understood as nice, a nice person has to want to help. Whoever says he is nice but does not want to help people is not a nice person, though it is reflected in something separate.

blocks.question: Why did we use that example of the apple's color?
blocks.text:
The color is not connected to the taste; it only symbolizes it. So too wanting to do a nice thing here: seemingly you are nice regardless, and wanting to help this person has nothing to do with what you are; you could be nice and just not show it. That holds only until *Adam Kadmon* associates the two. Then, to be nice, you have to do these things; it is essential. That is the *ratzon l'ratzon*: it *mamash* becomes associated.

All this is the *mashal*; the subject is G-d, going from *Adam Kadmon* to *Atzilus*.

In *Adam Kadmon* G-d chose the general way He is revealed, His self-image, His essential character: through ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes). That is not for any reason; nothing He does has to be for a reason. It is that way because He wants it.

So everything in *Adam Kadmon* is like *sechel*. G-d is higher than the limits of intellect and of a system, but because He chooses that there be a system, there is one, and it becomes real. *Adam Kadmon* is the source of nature and all these things.

G-d chose to reveal Himself through being logical, but you see that it is by His choice. That is the essence of the *sefiros*, the way they connect to G-d: He wants to reveal Himself as wise. Really He is above wisdom, yet He wants it to come in a way the intellect will make sense of and appreciate; the same with creating everything. In *Adam Kadmon* G-d chooses to make these things G-dly attributes, but inherently they are not connected to Him any more than anything else.

Why should these be G-dly attributes? We call G-d omnipotent, omniscient and omnificent, but only after *Adam Kadmon*. Before that we cannot say He is all-knowing or creates infinitely, because G-d is far beyond intellect and being a creator: to Him "it's not any more of a praise to say that He's all-knowing than it is to say that He's like all-stupid." So why should we see G-dliness in His being a creator?

In *Adam Kadmon* G-d chose a *ratzon* of a *ratzon*. The essential will is to reveal His essence in the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). He connected it to the particular wills of the *sefiros*: to reveal Himself through His wisdom; a logical system; creating everything, and so that it appears independent; miracles and *tzaddikim* (the righteous); giving everything its sustenance; a world that seems to run on its own; individualized attention over everything; and the limits of time and space. Those are the ten *sefiros*. And He is the *Malchus* (kingship): He decided to reveal Himself as the master, who controls everything.

Once G-d decided this is a G-dly attribute, He has to control everything. Now He has to want to control earthworms, tell them what to do, impose His dominion on them, because now that proves His G-dliness. Essentially it does not, but having chosen it, it is intrinsically bound to Him.

He could have let you create some things. He made it that He has His hands in every single thing, creating it every moment, and that is how He proves His G-dliness to us.

The creating is the *chesed* (kindness) of *Adam Kadmon*. That G-d creates everything every moment is the light of *Atzilus* that comes out after *Adam Kadmon*: just a *gilui*, like a color, revealing that He chose to be a creator. Once He chose that, creating everything becomes essential to Him, and He wills it in an infinite way.

sections.title: The lights come from the essential letters: the Names of Adam Kadmon
sections.summary: Because G-d chose a form to reveal Himself in, the letters of *Adam Kadmon*, the infinite lights of the ten *sefiros* come to be: *Ayin Beis*, a *milui* of *yuds*, sees every particular as a real piece of the whole, and *SaG*, with its *alef*, appreciates G-d by comparing. Like the lowest level of the soul's form, these Names work like a function: once G-d chose them, the world has to run in a certain order.

phrases.he: ולכך כל התהוות אורות דעשר ספירות
phrases.en: therefore the whole creation of the lights of the ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: הן באים מבחינת אותיות עצמיים דמאצילן
phrases.en: come from the letters, the essential letters of the *ma'atzil*, from *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: Therefore the whole creation of the lights of the ten *sefiros* comes **from the letters, the essential letters** of the *ma'atzil*, *Adam Kadmon*. G-d chose to reveal Himself in a certain form, the letters of *Adam Kadmon*, and that creates the lights of *Atzilus*: the infinite lights behind the ten *sefiros* come to be only once G-d chooses to associate Himself with certain ideas.

Since G-d chose to associate Himself with wisdom, that creates the infinite light: G-d expressed through the wisdom in everything, so that it reveals Him. Connected to Him, it becomes a great will that everything must have wisdom in it, and it takes on G-dly qualities, essential, axiomatic, infinite: the lights of the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: וכמו שם ע''ב,
phrases.en: for example the name *Ayin Beis*

phrases.he: שממנו בא בחינת אור החכמה דאצילות בגילוי

blocks.text:
**For example the name Ayin Beis** (seventy-two), the Name of *chachma*, through which G-d chose to reveal Himself as wise. Its spelling hints at the form of *chachma* G-d created: He not only associated Himself with wisdom, He also chose what wisdom is going to be, and the Name of 72 defines it.

Rabbi Walters says he does not understand the symbolism well enough to give a real definition of wisdom from it.

The general idea is a *milui* (the spelling out of a letter's name) of *yuds*. The form everything in creation follows, the form of man, is the four letters *yud*, *kei*, *vav*, *kei*: *tzimtzum* (contraction), *hispashtus* (spreading forth), *hamshacha* (drawing down) and *hispashtus*. That is the general form G-d chose.

Within it He created wisdom, the *milui* of *yuds*: you see all four, but everything in the way of *tzimtzum*, like the *yud*, which is just the *nekuda* (a point). You see anything as a little *prat* (a particular) representing a bigger *klal* (the whole).

blocks.title: The child, a piece of the father
blocks.text:
But it is an actual piece of it, like the drop of the father's brain: the child is actually a piece of the father, so he has all the father's qualities. So in *chachma*, which corresponds to *Atzilus*, eating an apple is an actual example, very small and contracted, of *chesed*, of the power to give life. Getting energy from eating is an actual experience of the *mahus* (what a thing is in itself) of giving life.

So you see everything as little examples of G-d Himself. That is the *chachma* through which G-d wants to reveal Himself, and it creates the light of *Ayin Beis* of *Atzilus*: the will that everything should, in an infinite way, express this relationship.

*Chachma* is seeing something as directly connected to the *klal* it represents, until it is *mamash* synonymous with it, a small taste of the *mahus* of the thing, totally transparent to what it expresses.

To see a big wisdom in music is to *mamash* get a little taste of a person's talent in it. A wise person who gives good advice saw in his experiences a lesson about the nature of reality, and sees that it is the same as what you are going through. That is the main thing of wisdom: deriving the *klal* from the *prat*.

blocks.title: One piece of chocolate
blocks.text:
You see the *prat* as *mamash* a *dugma* of the *klal*. It is a symbolic example, yet it actually contains the whole, as the *Mishna* has the whole *Gemara* in it. *Chachma* comes in a *kitzur* (shortening) but has everything. "Once you taste one piece of chocolate, you've experienced chocolate"; every chocolate is the same. That is unlike learning about something indirectly, through a *mashal*, which does not have everything.

So G-d created a relationship in which *chachma* sees everything as a small piece of G-d, a little example of Him. That is the beginning of the *chachma* of *Atzilus*, in revelation.

phrases.he: הרי זה
phrases.en: so that's like the way that the name represents that

phrases.he: שם המורה על עצם דחכמה דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: So the name *Ayin Beis*, the name 72 represents the essential name of *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: וכן שם ס''ג המורה על עצם אור דבינה דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: and the same thing with the name of 63, which represents the essential light of *bina* of *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: **So that's like the way that the name represents that**: the letters show that G-d chose to reveal Himself through that kind of name. *Ayin Beis*, 72, is the essential name of *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*: G-d's choice to be wise and what that means, His picture of how He wants to be revealed as wise. From it comes the light of *chachma*.

**And the same thing with the name of 63**, *SaG*, the essential light of *bina* (understanding) of *Adam Kadmon*. It is almost the same as *chachma*, except that in the middle, the *hamshacha*, there is an *alef* instead of a *yud*. Here you see the essential point through a relative thing, G-d's greatness by comparing Him with other things. The *alef* is made like a scale, two points with a line in the middle, to compare and contrast: if He can create this, He must surely be greater. It is appreciating the essence through something else.

phrases.he: והן ע''ב ס''ג כו' שלפני עשר ספירות דאצילות,
phrases.en: so these names 72, 63, 45 and 52, the names of *Adam Kadmon*, which are before the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: ונקרא שמות המאציל כו'
phrases.en: those are called the names of the Emanator.

blocks.text: These Names, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, 72, 63, 45 and 52, are the Names of *Adam Kadmon*, **which are before the ten sefiros of Atzilus**. **Those are called the names of the Emanator**, *shmos hama'atzil*: just the way G-d chose to reveal Himself.

phrases.he: וכמו בחינת האחרונה שבצורה הרוחניות
phrases.en: this is like the most external level of the spiritual form

phrases.he: שמקושר אל תחילת התהוות האור והצורה בכלי החומר כו'
phrases.en: which is connected to the beginning of the creation of the light and the form in the vessel when it comes into actual matter

blocks.text:
**This is like the most external level of the spiritual form**, connected to the beginning of the light and form in the vessel when it comes into matter, as said before: as the soul develops and grows, so does the body, which must fit the soul. The eye is made to be a vessel for seeing, the brain for understanding. Since seeing already has a definition, in the physical world it must come in certain ways.

So too wisdom has a definition. Our world's circumstances are totally separate from it, but put the two together and it is like a function: "once you have the input and the function, the product is automatic."

blocks.title: Input, function, product
blocks.text:
*Adam Kadmon* is like making a function, a system for how you interface with the world. Plug in a stimulus and the result is essential; it has to come out a certain way. Once you have defined yourself as kind, or whatever kind of person, in a given situation you have to act in a way that reflects it, or you are not being who you want to be.

So once G-d chose to reveal Himself through a certain thing, the world has to work a certain way to reveal Him. Certain things will and certain things will not, and so the world runs in a certain order.

Of course, since He has choice, He can always change things. But within the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) there is a level where it is a system. That is why things seem natural, and on a higher level, why one can know what G-d wants, like astrology.

blocks.title: The astrologer and the hammer
blocks.text: Astrology is really a Jewish wisdom: knowing the names of G-d, you see what goes on in the world, plug it into the names and figure out what G-d would want to do. Stars set up a certain way are like a person taking out a hammer. The *goyishe* (gentile) astrologers conclude that he is probably going to bang in a nail, or, to be more correct, since he may be pulling one, that it has something to do with a nail. That is so general that they are right most of the time; but he could be using the hammer for something that has nothing to do with a nail, so sometimes they are totally wrong.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the astrologers of the nations "goyishe", a Yiddish word that can read as dismissive in print.

blocks.text: Those are the tools through which He does things. Before the final product, G-d gets out the tools. When the weather turns, a certain guy goes into power, the stock market takes a turn, you can guess the general way things usually go, like the weathermen: usually right in general, sometimes totally wrong. But if you understand what G-d wants to accomplish, the names behind the vessels, you see exactly what He wants to do. If you knew what a person wanted to do and saw him take out the tool, you would know what he was going to do with it.

No, not in a mechanistic, deterministic way; even the weather is not mechanistic like that. And looking in the stars does not mean only the stars. It means looking at the way things are turning, everything: the way they would interpret events.

blocks.title: The hurricane that would not hit Florida
blocks.text:
When a hurricane heads for Florida, the weather people say it will hit full force, so evacuate. The Rebbe understood that, for whatever reason, G-d would not want it to hit that place, and said there was no need even to bother evacuating; it was not going to happen. He saw that this could not be the purpose of the hurricane.

By the Rebbe it is even higher: he did not figure it out that way. He is *mamash* in on the plan; "the Rebbe can decide what's going to happen."

Even a regular kabbalist or *tzaddik* can sometimes know such things: something is impossible because it is not in G-d's plan, and G-d would not do it. Even if, by the vessel, it looks like it will happen, if it does not match the name it will not.

It is like a nice guy you know cares for you: if he does something that looks against your benefit, you know there is no way he would, and you can trust that, though it looks that way. The name is the expression of oneself. If you understand what G-d wants to express, you see what is going to happen.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בדם הוא הנפש
phrases.en: Like we said before, about how the soul goes into the blood

phrases.he: ובצמיחה הרוחנית
phrases.en: and like the spiritual growth going into the physical growth

phrases.he: ובעין ומוח כו'
phrases.en: in the eye and the mind

blocks.text: **Like we said before, about how the soul goes into the blood**, **the spiritual growth going into the physical growth**, and **the eye and the mind**: the physical form has to work a certain way to be a vessel for the spiritual form of these powers, only because the spiritual power already has a form. Before it had one, in theory, it could work without it.

Our brain is set up like a very complicated computer, a vessel for thinking. Had G-d wanted, a mushy blob of clay could have been a good vessel for thinking. He did not do that; although in a way He did, since our brain kind of is that mushy blob. "It is really a joke that the brain thinks": the brain is stupid, just wet, mushy slop.

The spiritual form gets connected to the shape of the vessel, like the cat: whatever it eats turns into a cat, because its soul imposes the cat form on it. So the spiritual form of growth makes the tree, the power of seeing makes the eye a vessel that can see, and the power of thought makes the mind a vessel that can think.

sections.title: The vessel: chachma in the brain of Atzilus, a separate power called wisdom
sections.summary: The vessel that limits the light of *chachma* is like the intellect already blended into the brain, which gets only the thickening of its end. In the vessel, G-d's inherent relationship to everything becomes "wisdom", a power we can name and point to, like the Torah; to define G-d by such attributes is what makes the philosophers' question of evil.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת הכלי המגביל האור דחכמה דאצילות,
phrases.en: However, the vessel that limits the light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: הוא כמו אור השכל שממוזג כבר בחומר המוח
phrases.en: That's like the way that the *sechel* already goes into the brain.

phrases.he: שחומר המוח מקבל רק מהתעבות סוף אור השכל
phrases.en: that the brain only gets the thickening of the end of the light of the intellect.

blocks.text: Now the *nimshal*. G-d wanted to reveal Himself in a certain way, the spiritual form, and that imposes a form on the world, to be a fitting vessel for it. **However, the vessel that limits the light** of *chachma* of *Atzilus* is like the intellect already blended in the matter of the brain: **the way that the sechel already goes into the brain**.

**The brain only gets the thickening of the end of the light of the intellect**, the *hisabus*: only the part of the intellect that relates to physical things. At a certain level the spiritual concept of intellect can be represented by patterns, expressed by different orders of neuron flashes. The vessel of *chachma* of *Atzilus* is like the brain, and its light is like the soul's power of intellect.

phrases.he: על כן מגבילו,
phrases.en: therefore it limits it

phrases.he: מלבד שינוי המהות כו'
phrases.en: besides changing its *mahus*

phrases.he: כך הוא אור החכמה כשמתלבש במוחא, ונקרא חכמה מוחא כו'
phrases.en: So too, the light of G-d's wisdom when it goes into the vessel called *mocha*, the brain of *Atzilus*, and then it's called *chachma mocha*

blocks.text:
**Therefore it limits it**, **besides changing its mahus**. **So too, the light of G-d's wisdom** in the vessel called *mocha*, the brain of *Atzilus*, is called *chachma mocha*: limited, its *mahus* changed.

*Chachma* as it is in *Adam Kadmon* is that everything is G-d, the world just a little example of His being; that could be said of everything in the world. In *Atzilus* G-d chose to reveal His *chachma* through a vessel, in certain things and not others, so that we see certain things as *chachma* and certain things as *chesed*: a distinction.

So G-d created, not yet the Torah, just the *chachma* of *Atzilus*: an idea of divine wisdom, that things will be logical and graceful, with patterns and a reason. Revealed in that, G-d becomes like a super intellect, G-dly but related to what we call intellect, limited. Now it is seen as wisdom, not as a revelation of G-d. Instead of inherent in everything, it is an ability G-d has: you see His wisdom in the world, His power to make things in the most perfect, beautiful way.

Before the vessel, the light of wisdom was an inherent truth about G-d, His relationship with the world because of His being, and so a revelation of Him. In the vessel of *chachma* of *Atzilus* it becomes a separate power.

blocks.title: A kid spilled the ink
blocks.text:
So you see it as a different *metzius* (existence): wisdom, not G-d. G-d reveals Himself indirectly, by being the smartest of anybody. The wisdom in a tree or in DNA, the way the cells work, is far greater than anything human, so we say it must have come from G-d. Wisdom is already seen as severed from G-d, but it is so amazing that only G-d could have done it; the design could not be an accident.

If the world were simpler, we could say it was an accident: "A kid spilled the ink." Since it is so amazing, it must be intelligent, and only somebody as intelligent as G-d.

Look deeper and it is not even like that. Inherently the world must have been created by G-d or it could not exist; nothing makes itself. Even the ink, the paper and the spilling could not start without prior things; the scenario already makes assumptions. But we work under those assumptions and limits, so even here it is revealed through the vessel of wisdom.

phrases.he: שאז מצד בחינת כלי החכמה הוא בא בשם מציאות דבר שכל,
phrases.en: So then, because of this vessel of *chachma*, the light becomes something that you can call an intellect.

phrases.he: הנקרא התחכמות דבר מה בפרט
phrases.en: actually coming up with a particular idea

blocks.text: **Because of this vessel of chachma, the light becomes something that you can call an intellect**: you can say that G-d is wise. *Hu hamada v'hu hayodea v'hu hayadua* (He is the knowledge, the knower and the known), and G-d as omnipotent, omniscient, omnificent, omnipresent: those are the vessels of *Atzilus*, as the soul in the body becomes the power of movement and of seeing.

But the soul itself is much higher than moving a body and lifting things, or even thinking and seeing; it is not limited to physical perception and thought. It has a form, but it does not relate to these limits. So too G-d created the vessel, a tool, these limits, wisdom and the rest, and reveals Himself by being the ultimate of them, by showing how He can use them, the way you show yourself by showing how you use your brain.
That is how you show who you are: you show your personality and everything. And G-d shows it by showing how He uses the same ten *sefiros*.

Most people define G-d that way: a being who is omnipotent, omniscient and all those things. That is not true. To say that is G-d is just saying He is a big person. He is much higher; He only chose to express Himself through them. In fact, in philosophy the main proofs against G-d's existence come from those definitions.

blocks.title: How could a wise G-d create stupidity?
blocks.text:
Defining G-d that way, one could ask: if G-d is the ultimate of wisdom, how can there be stupidity in the world? He does not know whether they thought of that; what they actually ask is how a good G-d could create evil. It is the same question, only "nobody cares that there's stupidity that much."

So the fallacy is not really about evil. They define G-d as one of two sides of a coin. Wisdom implies stupidity; once G-d is the ultimate of something relative, His existence implies its opposite, and their definition creates the question.

blocks.title: The premise makes the question
blocks.text:
Calling G-d the ultimate in goodness already assumes good and bad, so you cannot then ask how bad can exist: you assumed it before you started. Defining G-d as only good accepts a prior axiom, good and evil, that exists before G-d. Then evil must be able to exist, since you made G-d's existence depend on both, and you cannot disprove Him by it.

The conclusion should not be that G-d does not exist, but that their definition is bad. Logic dictates an intelligent creator; they define what He must be, then use the definition to show He cannot exist. That only shows the definition is flawed; it does not uproot the original proof that there must be a creator.

People often do not know how to use logic. They reach a fallacy, do not know what the problem was, and come to crazy conclusions without realizing they are confusing themselves. They take the logical system they set up as a real thing that works, because they never thought of questioning their axioms, which they chose based on prior things that could be flawed.

sensitivity.reason: Says of the philosophers who argue against G-d that they do not know how to use logic and come to crazy conclusions.
sensitivity.publishable: They reach a fallacy, do not know what the problem was, and come to these conclusions without realizing they are confusing themselves. They take the logical system they set up as a real thing that works, because they never thought of questioning their axioms, which they chose based on prior things that could be flawed.

blocks.text: That is how the human intellect works in the brain: then you can call it intellect, **actually coming up with a particular idea**. Before the vessel of *chachma* there is only the inherent reality of G-d's relationship to any creation, from His nature. In the vessel you can ask G-d for an example of His wisdom, and then you have the Torah, particular wisdom out of the vessel of *chachma*. Before that there could be no book of particular teachings; it would be a pervasive reality, not something you could point at.

sections.title: Three governors and four Names: the vessel is made from the thickening of the light
sections.summary: The heart and the liver are vessels like the brain: G-d's modes of conduct and His sustaining of the world, as emotions are felt in the heart and life works through digestion. These three rulers are the letters of the lights, the four Names of *Atzilus*, made from the light's thickening, as a chair takes the shape of the one who sits and a cup the shape of the wish to drink; that is the light's *yeshus*.

phrases.he: וכן המדות הרוחניים בלבא
phrases.en: the same thing, the spiritual emotions in the heart

phrases.he: והנפש הרוחניות בכבדא כו'

blocks.text: **The same thing, the spiritual emotions in the heart.** G-d creates systems for how He relates to the world, modes of conduct, being strict and being nice, and those are the vessel for His relationships with the world, the inherent lights of the *middos* (emotional attributes). And the liver: a way of sustaining the world, constantly building it up to keep its form. Those are the external emotions, G-d's external relationship to the world, revealed through Him as provider of sustenance.

The *mashal* of our heart, in its details, comes later. For now: in the vessel it changes from spiritual to physical. Our emotions, going from the soul to the heart, are felt in a certain way: we experience love and fear through the heart. And our life is expressed through the liver, through digestion, using energy and expelling waste, a physical process that builds the body into a form. That is the soul's level of *Asiya* (the world of Action), the *nefesh*: the liver.

It is not defined by the body; it comes from an inner spiritual power. Eating, needing nutrients, the whole way the body works, is totally circumstantial to the soul, which just pushes the body into being its vessel. But the body, the DNA, the blood, the liver, is much more limited, and it limits the soul: you can eat only certain things, and the soul can turn only certain things into the body, because it works through the liver, and the liver works a certain way. As far as the soul is concerned, "it could be a soul of a tree," doing it differently with a different vessel.

phrases.he: והן ענין ג' שליטין לעילה,
phrases.en: these three vessels, the brain, the heart and the liver, are called the three governors above

phrases.he: בחינת ג' כלים כללים לנר''נ דזעיר אנפין דאצילות
phrases.en: These are the three general vessels for the *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama* of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: נשמה, שהוא בחינת מוחין דחכמה ובינה שבזעיר אנפין במוחא,
phrases.en: the *neshama*, which is the intellect, the mind of *chachma* and *bina* of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, goes into the brain

phrases.he: ורוח בלבא כו'
phrases.en: and the *ruach* goes in the heart, and the *nefesh* goes into the liver.

blocks.text: These three vessels, **the brain, the heart and the liver, are called the three governors above**: the vessels that govern everything. G-d created a form for revealing the consciousness of G-dliness, the brain; for His interaction with the world, good and bad, conscious care and direction, the heart; and for providing basic needs, making the world, its design and upkeep, the liver. Since He does these in certain ways, certain things make us conscious of certain aspects of that relationship, and others of others.

**These are the three general vessels for the nefesh, ruach, neshama** (the three levels of the soul) **of Zeir Anpin** (lit. the small countenance) **of Atzilus**. **The neshama, which is the intellect**, the *mochin* (lit. brains) of *chachma* and *bina*, **goes into the brain**; **the ruach goes in the heart, and the nefesh goes into the liver**.

phrases.he: והן האותיות דאורות דאצילות,
phrases.en: these vessels are the letters of the lights of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שזהו ענין ד' שמות ע''ב ס''ג דאצילות כו'
phrases.en: These are the four names *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH*, *BaN* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שנקרא כלים לעשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: these are called the vessels for the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: המגבילים האור ומצמצמו,
phrases.en: that they limit the light, and they contract it

phrases.he: לפי שמהתעבות האור נעשה הכלי,
phrases.en: because the vessel comes from the thickening of the light.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*

blocks.text: **These vessels are the letters of the lights of Atzilus**: **the four names Ayin Beis, SaG, MaH, BaN of Atzilus**. G-d defined His revelation through these four Names, and the letters of each define how it works, so that *chachma* gets one definition, *bina* another. **These are called the vessels for the ten sefiros of Atzilus**. They **limit the light, and they contract it**, **because the vessel comes from the thickening of the light**.
Really G-d could reveal Himself in any way, but since He chose a concrete, specific way, narrowing it down to that specific thing, that narrowing makes the vessel.

blocks.title: The chair and the cup
blocks.text:
"The shape of a chair comes from your rear end." Your body already has a form, so you are comfortable in certain positions; put into tangible form, that dictates the chair. Your desire to drink, put into the way water and materials work, creates the form of a cup. That is why all cups have certain things in common: within our world's limits, an effective vessel needs a certain form, because your desire already has one.

So too G-d first creates the form of how He wants to reveal Himself, the light, like your desire to sit or drink, then a limitation, the vessel, like the way the world works. Together, the light shapes the matter into a good vessel for it.

So G-d made the soul and gave matter a certain form; for the soul to express itself through matter, the matter has to be built into a body. Both sides of the coin, the advantage of the light and that of the vessel, come soon, though probably not in this chapter. These letters are the vessels of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, which limit the light, **like it says in Etz Chaim**.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא בחינת הישות של האור,
phrases.en: This is called the ego of the light, the somethingness of the light, the tangibleness of it.

phrases.he: כשנראה לבחינת יש ודבר מה במציאות
phrases.en: when it seems to be like a distinct entity.

phrases.he: כידוע ודי למבין

blocks.text: **This is called the ego of the light, the somethingness of the light, the tangibleness of it**, its *yeshus*: **when it seems to be like a distinct entity**. When G-d reveals Himself in a form and it seems that this is who He is, so that you can define Him by it, that is the vessel. You can say G-d is wise, omnipotent, omniscient, because He put Himself into the vessel of those things as if it were a body.

Just as I point to a person's body and say his name, because his soul is in that vessel, so G-d reveals Himself through these vessels as if that is who He is, and it becomes a *yeshus*. That is the source of the perception of bad, as was explained a little.

sections.title: Two kinds of Names, and praying to the light
sections.summary: There are two sets of Names, one in *Adam Kadmon* before *Atzilus* and one after it as the limiting vessels; so one who intends the Names should intend their source, the light, and the vessel follows by itself. In prayer this means asking for what G-d wants to reveal, not for the winning ticket: *emuna*, and the way to be *mechaven* in *Shmone Esreh*.

phrases.he: (ונמצא ב' מיני שמות ע''ב ס''ג כו'
phrases.en: so it comes out there's two types of names, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH*, *BaN*.

phrases.he: א' לפני האצילות
phrases.en: one before *Atzilus*, in *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: והב' אחר האצילות
phrases.en: one lower than the light of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שהן הכלים המגבילים
phrases.en: which are the vessels that limit the light of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: **So it comes out there's two types of names, Ayin Beis, SaG, MaH, BaN**: **one before Atzilus, in Adam Kadmon**, and **one lower than the light of Atzilus**, **which are the vessels that limit the light of Atzilus**.

phrases.he: ולפי זה
phrases.en: based on this

phrases.he: המכוין בשמות
phrases.en: when somebody intends to the names

phrases.he: מכוין במקור האורות
phrases.en: you should intend to the source of the light

phrases.he: כמו מכוין בבחינת שם ע''ב, מקור לאור החכמה כו',
וממילא הוא מכוון בכלי החכמה,
phrases.en: automatically you'll be *mechaven b'kli hachachma*

phrases.he: שיומשך למטה כו' ודי למבין

blocks.text: **Based on this, when somebody intends to the names, you should intend to the source of the light**. When you pray, have in mind what G-dly revelation G-d is trying to reveal through the vessel of *chachma*, and see past the vessel. Do not ask G-d to make things come out a certain way. It is beyond that: once you clarify the light G-d is trying to reveal, it will come out properly in the right vessel by itself.

It imposes its form on the vessel automatically, and **automatically you'll be mechaven** (intending) **b'kli hachachma**, in the vessel of *chachma*. To understand the Torah, try to see past it into the G-dliness behind it, and you will understand it properly. That is why learning Torah for its own sake gives you understanding: you get the real thing behind it. Sensitive to what G-d is trying to reveal, you put it into the intellect right, because you know the real goal.

blocks.title: Talking to the ear
blocks.text: Talking to somebody, you have to talk to his ear, but the ear is only the external vessel; you want him to understand. Focus on making him understand, and you will control your voice so his ear hears: you look at his face, and if it seems he cannot hear you, you adjust without thinking. So if you are *mechaven* to the light, you will be *mechaven* to the vessel, without having to worry about it.

blocks.title: "Could you help me?"
blocks.text: And when you ask somebody for something there are two ways: ask him to reach in his pocket and give you a dollar, or ask him to help you. Then he will do whatever he can to help, and figure out on his own how to do it.

So when you pray, do not be *mechaven* to winning the *Tan Yad* auction: that is the vessel. Be *mechaven* to why G-d would want to give it to you: to take care of you, or more, to reveal G-dliness, so that you will do *mivtzoim* or whatever it is. Focus on that inner *kavana* (intention) and G-d will give you whatever you need for it. You do not worry about the vessel, because you do not really care how it comes out. You do not really want the money; you want not to worry about *parnasa* (livelihood), so you can pray and do what you need to. Ask G-d for that, and everything will be set up for it.

This is called *emuna* (faith): you trust that G-d will make everything come out for the best, and let Him take care of the vessel. You are *mechaven* only to the inner thing: my job is Torah and *mitzvos*, and G-d knows what is best for me and will figure out how to help. Later comes *bitachon* (trust), an opposite *avoda* (divine service), which focuses on the *kli* (vessel).

phrases.he: והיינו כוונות שמות דח''י ברכות שמונה עשרה
phrases.en: This is the way you should be *mechaven* the names in *Shmone Esreh*

phrases.he: כי הא בהא תליא, משום דשורש הכלים המגבילים משמות דעצמות המאציל, כמו שיתבאר ודי למבין)

blocks.text: **This is the way you should be mechaven the names in Shmone Esreh** (the eighteen blessings): to the inner thing. As a discourse says, do not just ask for a physical thing; in the blessing for the year, ask for a year successful in praying and learning. Some places say to be *mechaven* *davka* (specifically) to the spirituality of the blessings and not ask for the physical; others imply you *davka* ask for the physical, which a later chapter takes up. Really it is both: first be *mechaven* to the spiritual; once you recognize that, you can go back to asking for the physical.

Since the vessels come from the light, once you are *mechaven* to the light the vessels come out good. That is why, when you nullify yourself more to G-d, to Torah and *mitzvos*, and do His mission, He gives you all the blessings so you can do it properly: money, health, no worries, children.

That is the main *kavana* of *Shmone Esreh*, and why it follows the *Shema*. If in the *Shema* you are *mechaven* to *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice), to accept the yoke of heaven and of the *mitzvos*, G-d answers you in *Shmone Esreh*: you ask in order to spread G-dliness, so you are a good vessel, and G-d wants to give, because it is not a waste. What goes against the *kavana* He will not give, since it would be wasted. Really G-d loves us and gives us things, and there is more going on here, but that is the idea.

sections.title: Tikunim: the eye is the soul's glasses
sections.summary: The vessels are also called *tikunim*, garments that fix: as glasses, a telescope or a microscope fix the eye to see further, the physical eye fixes the soul's power of sight to focus on physical things.

phrases.he: והיינו מה שכתוב וקרינן לון י' ספירין כו'
phrases.en: and this is what it says in *Tikunei Zohar*, that G-d called them ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: לאחזאה לאנהגא כו',
phrases.en: to reveal Himself, and to conduct the world

phrases.he: כי תיקונין הן בחינת הכלים לאורות דאצילות
phrases.en: the garments are the vessels to the lights of *Atzilus*

blocks.text: At the end of chapter 28 the subject is *tikunim* (garments). What is the difference between a *kli* and a *tikun*? *Tikunei Zohar* says **that G-d called them ten sefiros**, **to reveal Himself, and to conduct the world**: He brought out ten *tikunim*, garments, and called them the ten *sefiros*. So **the garments are the vessels to the lights of Atzilus**, but a little differently from before.

phrases.he: וכמו על דרך משל תיקון העין,
phrases.en: for example, like the way that you fix up the eye

phrases.he: שיתפשט ראיה גשמית שבו יותר,
phrases.en: that its physical sight should go further

phrases.he: הוא על ידי אמצעות כלי ההבטה כו'
phrases.en: is through a vessel for seeing, either a telescope or a microscope or regular glasses.

phrases.he: כך תיקון התפשטות ראיה הרוחניות על ידי אמצעות כלי העין הגשמי כו'
phrases.en: So too the physical eye is like the glasses for the soul.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר
phrases.en: as explained elsewhere

blocks.title: Glasses for the soul
blocks.text:
**For example, like the way that you fix up the eye**, **that its physical sight should go further**: it **is through a vessel for seeing, either a telescope or a microscope or regular glasses**. A *tikun* fixes the thing, as the word means: it helps it do what it could not normally do.

**So too the physical eye is like the glasses for the soul.** The soul really has the power of sight; the eye channels it to physical things, the way a telescope channels your sight to a faint, far-away star or a microscope to something very small.

blocks.title: What a telescope does
blocks.text: The only problem is that the lens of your eye does not focus that well; your power of sight is no different. All a telescope does is take the light hitting a lens five inches wide and focus it onto your eye, a quarter or an eighth of an inch. Many times more light hits your eye, and you can see something too small for your eye's resolution, or too faint.

blocks.title: Pixels per degree
blocks.text: A microscope does the same: it blows up the image so your eye can notice the details, which really you could see. Your eye has only a certain resolution, about 288 pixels per degree of vision in your main vision, fewer in the periphery, and something too small "will just slip in between the pixels of your eyes." Blow up the image and you see it. You only have to fix your eye to focus on that kind of thing.

blocks.question: Are you fixing the eye, or are you fixing the image?
blocks.text: It does not really matter; it is the same thing, and in a way the student is right. You fix the image so it can focus in the eye; it is a two-way thing. On the other hand, the eye is trying to see, and you refocus it so it can. **As explained elsewhere.**

sections.title: Through the limiting vessels the light comes down: kli and tikun
sections.summary: Only in the limiting vessels can the light be drawn down: an idea settled in the mind reaches the emotions and other people, love in the heart reaches a receiver. A *kli* holds the whole power at rest, like the body for the soul; a *tikun* transforms it into one particular expression, like a uniform, so that we can see G-d without being burned. In the essential light the *sefiros* are still *b'li ma*: G-d's wisdom and creating are infinite in everything, and seen in a tree only as a glimmer of a glimmer.

phrases.he: על כן מצד בחינת הכלים המגבילים, על ידי זה דוקא יוכל להיות כל בחינת השפעות והמשכות למטה מטה
phrases.en: Therefore, specifically when the light goes into the vessels that limit the light, it's able to be revealed down to the physical world.

phrases.he: וכמו על ידי כלי המוח שישיג השכל, ימשיכנו להמדות
phrases.en: So therefore, if through the mind grasping the *sechel*, an intellect, it's able to bring it down to the emotions

phrases.he: או להשפיעו לזולתו
phrases.en: or it can be explained to someone else.

blocks.text: **Therefore, specifically when the light goes into the vessels that limit the light, it's able to be revealed down to the physical world.** So, **through the mind grasping the sechel**, **it's able to bring it down to the emotions**, **or it can be explained to someone else**. To explain something, even to yourself, or to feel it, you have to understand it well. You can hold something by *emuna* and feel it, without its settling into the vessel of your mind; once it does, you can bring it down to yourself or to someone else.

That is one of the main things of learning *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching). A Jew has an essential *emuna* in G-d; studying brings it into his feelings and actions, and to other people. That happens only in the *kli*; otherwise the light is not fixed and you do not know how to focus it. You can believe in G-d and not know what to do about it until you learn the Torah: G-d wants this, so do this and not that. Even belief itself: what does it mean for how you relate to the world?

blocks.question: How can the soul see without the eye?
blocks.text: It is just not a physical sight. You are used to physical sight, so that is what you call sight. Real sight is perceiving an essence directly: the soul in the Garden of Eden perceives G-dliness in a way of *re'iya* (sight). And you dream without your eye, and see things. The eye just triggers the first perceptions, because it contracts the *koach* (power), but the *koach* is in you before that.

blocks.question: Well, you still need your brain?
blocks.text: Not really. You are only used to being conscious within your body, and do not know what it is like to be just a soul. Just as you do not need your eye, you do not need your brain; and when the soul leaves the body it still carries its memories of the world. The example given is the Garden of Eden, "but, you know, who knows about that."

The soul before it goes into the *kli* is the *mashal* for before *Atzilus*. There the lights of G-dliness are all hidden, like your soul before your body: the essential lights of G-d, which you cannot know, *ilu yedativ hayisiv* (if I knew Him, I would be Him), totally infinite. How can you know what a soul is before the body? We have no *hasaga* (comprehension) of the *mahus* of our own soul, only through our body.

As our soul is hidden when it is not in our body, G-dliness is hidden when it is not in the vessels of *Atzilus*, so much so that it is called *Radla*, the head that does not know: it does not even know what it is. It is not revealed, not yet a known thing.

blocks.question: We already know it is a hidden thing; what is there to know about it?
blocks.text: That is exactly what it is: a hidden thing, and that is exactly what we are trying to know. Not what it is as a revealed thing, but what a hidden thing is. The *mashal* is our soul before it comes into the body, and we know what that is: a hidden thing. For now we are only trying to understand the relationship.

There it is totally hidden, like the soul before the body; you cannot even speak of sight yet. Before the eye there are dreams, since the eye obviously only triggers it. Even the brain: consciousness must come from the soul, "because the brain is just a bunch of dirt." So even now you are seeing your soul itself, through the vessel. When you experience consciousness you have a *hasaga* of the essence of your soul; it is *mamash* your soul itself, since only the soul can be conscious.

The *nimshal*: before *Atzilus* G-d reveals Himself in essential lights. They include the ten *sefiros*, but what you perceive is only that He can do anything and is beyond limits. So He also has *chachma*, but you do not define Him as wise the way we know it.

In the vessel of *Atzilus*, G-d expresses His infinite abilities. Asked whether He can really do anything, He shows it: He can be infinitely wise, infinitely kind, and create infinitely. Something from nothing shows that only G-d could do it, but already through a specific vessel.

It is a vessel too, the one vessel of *Akudim*, with ten things in one vessel. That it is all one is like the will: G-d can do whatever He wants, one vessel that includes everything. That, by the way, is the source of the Jews: we come from that one vessel, still *b'li ma*, not from the particular things, from the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought), the one thought that includes everything.

Within the *hishtalshelus*, the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will) is to reveal that He can do anything. That is not the ultimate thing; it is *mishleimus koach maasav u'peulosav*, from the perfection of the power of His deeds and actions, *l'achzaa*, to reveal Himself to people. The ultimate thing is the *dira b'tachtonim*, the revelation of the Essence, and *davka* through our *avoda*.

phrases.he: וכן על ידי אמצעות כלי הלב לאור האהבה והחסד הרוחני,
phrases.en: the same way that when the light of love and kindness goes into your physical heart

phrases.he: יבא לכלל השפעה למקבל כידוע
phrases.en: then it relates to giving it out to a *mekabel*.

blocks.text: The vessel lets you bring it all the way down. **The same way that when the light of love and kindness goes into your physical heart, then it relates to giving it out to a mekabel** (receiver). In the heart it becomes a motivation to act, and so love and kindness are expressed in the physical world. But those are physical symptoms, the body's reaction to love, wanting to be close and to give. Love is not really in the heart, nor in the brain; it comes through there.

Everything goes through the brain first. That is why it is called *rosh* (head), as in *Rosh HaShana* and *Rosh Chodesh*: it includes everything, and from there it divides out. Scientists laugh at the old-fashioned people who said love is in the heart, since taking out a certain part of the brain takes away the emotions. "But they're just haughty idiots," pumping themselves up as knowing better instead of trying to understand what is being said. It says here too that everything goes through the brain; then it is revealed in the heart, and any idiot knows that you feel love in your heart, in your breathing and your heart rate.

blocks.text: **Therefore, the vessels are called fixers**, *tikunim*: **through them there's hamshacha from Atzilus to Beriya** (the world of Creation). **And this revelation from Atzilus to Beriya is just to reveal Himself to man and to conduct the worlds.**

phrases.he: אבל מצד עצמות אור המאציל נקרא עשר ספירות בלי מה כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: but the way that they are in the essential light of the *ma'atzil*, they're called the ten spheres without any *mahus*, like I said before

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות:

blocks.text: **But the way that they are in the essential light of the ma'atzil, they're called the ten spheres without any mahus, like I said before**: you cannot really say what they are; they are not that limited.

So the vessels have two sides. The inner one: they are a place where the soul rests, your consciousness in your body, your intellect in your brain, your emotions in your heart, your biological life in your liver. Then they are called a *kli*. But when you use them, the brain to think an idea, the heart to feel an actual emotion, the liver to digest food, they are called *tikunim*, garments or fixers: they transform the light into something that relates to the physical world, so you can have an effect.

Your eye fixes your power of sight to see physical things; your brain fixes your consciousness to affect your body and come up with physical ideas; your power of movement can move physical things. As glasses fix the eye, here the soul is fixed, revealed in a limited way we can perceive. So when G-d reveals Himself through these vessels, He becomes a limited thing that we can actually understand and perceive.

A *kli* is just the way the light of the soul rests in a thing, as your consciousness rests in your brain. When it shines through the brain to become physical thoughts, it is a *tikun*: it does not only hold your soul, it brings it across to a lower level. So the vessels do two things: the light rests in them, and they transform it into something that can come down a level.

Your soul rests in your body, which lets you be alive. But that you can move things is already a *tikun*: your soul uses your body to relate to what is outside and lower than it, even to things that are not its vessel. There is a big difference: resting in the vessel, you *mamash* have the *etzem* there.

So an emotion in your heart does two things. It limits it, so you are conscious of a certain feeling: that is just the vessel. And it makes it something you can express to someone else. It gives you a defined character, like a name that makes you a distinct thing, and it lets you relate to others. First it is for you, then it comes out to someone else.

You do not understand an idea fully until it reaches your brain and you put it into words; then you are totally conscious of it, and you can also explain it. At first, though, it is only for you.

The main thing of the *kli* is not a particular expression but that it can be used for anything: that you can think with your brain is the *kli*. It is a *tikun* when you think a particular thing and it lets you bring that across. It brings across not your power to think but your particular idea. When your hand moves something, it gives it not the power of movement, only the particular movement. But your hand as a vessel for your power of movement is infinite: you can move whichever way you want.

blocks.text: The next chapter discusses the difference between a limit in potential, a *kli*, and a limit in actuality, a *tikun*. Later, in the thirties, comes how *osios* (letters) are called both *kelim* and *levushim* (garments): the same idea, the inner side a *kli* and the outer side a *levush*. That it can turn your power into a particular movement is a *tikun*; that your whole essential power can rest there is a *kli*. "A *kli* holds the whole thing and a *levush* is only one expression of it."

blocks.title: The fireman's hat and the store uniform
blocks.text: Put on a fireman's hat and coat and we see you as a fireman; a white coat and a stethoscope, and we see a doctor. Different clothes are different roles. They are not your *etzem*; they express one thing you do, *davka* how people should relate to you, like a uniform. In a store you know whom to ask because of the store uniform; otherwise you ask some customer, who tells you, "Oh, I'm sorry sir, I don't work here." There is an idea here, and now it has kind of become a lost thing.

blocks.title: How the Rebbe dressed
blocks.text:
The real idea of clothes is different. The Rebbe did not copy the Previous Rebbe's dress; actually he did not dress like him. As a chassid, wanting to be left alone, he *davka* dressed like somebody modern, and people left him alone. When he wanted people *davka* to come to him as the Rebbe, he dressed like a Rebbe.

It says that when *Moshiach* comes, the prophets will wear long coats, like the High Priest's garment, so people know to ask them questions. So the Rebbe said mentors and heads of yeshivas should wear long coats all day, every day.

blocks.text: Why? So people know whom to ask about these things. Some say they would rather not; they are humble, who are they? That is a kind of foolish humility. That is your job: if you want to do it well, wear the clothes, because they help; if you do not want that job, *davka* do not. And people not doing that job are afraid to take off the clothes, as if without them they would not be chassidim. But being a chassid is not wearing a long coat.

blocks.title: So we won't get burned
blocks.text: So at the Sea they saw G-d as a young warrior, and at the giving of the Torah as an old sage: He put on different clothes. That is *tikunim*. But in the *mashal* the clothes fix you; in the *nimshal* they fix us. A fireman wears heat protection against the fire, "but G-d puts on the clothes so we won't get burned by Him." In a way it is reversed.

blocks.text: In a way it is more like the eye or the brain: the idea is too big. If G-d were revealed as He is essentially, we would not feel separate from Him. So first the vessels just reveal G-d within them. That is why the vessels of *Atzilus* are still *Elokus* (G-dliness): His whole *etzem* can be revealed there; they still have free choice and can create *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing). So it is called the end and the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite), as will be explained.

blocks.text:
But they are also the source of the limit, the *memutza* (a middle) between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*: their outer side makes the actual limit in time and space. The vessel of *chesed* of *Atzilus*, the idea of Creator, reveals G-d's essence. But when He uses it to create something, the creation reveals Him and is limited.

So the vessels bridge the gap. Their inner side reveals His whole *etzem*, because only G-d could create; their outer side is a limited thing we could know. G-d's choosing to be a Creator gave creation a reason to exist: as an example of His ability to create, which is an example of Him.

blocks.text: That is the idea of the vessels: the inner side reveals the whole *etzem*, and the outer side gives *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* a place to exist as separate from G-d. But they are not really separate; they are seen as connected, though limited.

blocks.text: *Adam Kadmon* does not yet relate to particulars like a tree, but in a way it does. The great wisdom in every detail of a tree, the infinite wisdom you see in it, is like *chachma*. That it is an infinitely complex system, everything different, all the parts working together, no two the same, is more like *bina*.

blocks.text: Then there is the essential will: the tree wants to grow, to be a tree in a certain form. Why? Where does it think it is going? Close to the sun. Look at trees and plants and they seem like idiots, growing and growing for more light with no end, "a totally meaningless, useless thing"; the only one who benefits is us. So there is obviously a big push of will there, and it makes no sense that it is the tree's: you see G-d's will pushing the tree.

blocks.text:
And you see it created anew every second. Look into the tree: every moment all its molecules revert to nothing and come back into existence; at the atomic level you see that. In a lesser way, the plant has renewed energy every day, and every year it loses its leaves, kind of dies and comes back. Really it happens every moment, the more you see it on an essential, constant level.

He points that out because that is the main place you see the level of light he is talking about now: the lights of *Atzilus* before they go into the *kelim*.

blocks.text: What you see every day or every year is how it is already enclothed in *kelim*. The essential light, before the *kelim*, is infinite. Even scientifically, at the molecular or subatomic level, they see that every moment it is recreated. But that is not revealed in a vessel, so you have to look deeper to see it. What the limited vessel reveals is renewal every day and every year. The light before the vessel is that G-d gives it new life every single moment, in an infinite way.

blocks.text: A person has an infinite ability for intellect, which in the brain comes out in particular ideas. Even his desire to express intellect in everything he comes across, the infinite light that goes into the brain, comes from his *Adam Kadmon*: he decided he wants to be a smart person. So too, because G-d decided to reveal Himself through wisdom, there is an inherent light that wants to reveal His wisdom infinitely in everything. That is not manifest to us. Through the vessels it is manifest in limited ways, more in certain things than others, though if we think about it we realize G-d's wisdom is manifest infinitely in everything.

blocks.question: Rocks don't seem to have that renewal as much?
blocks.text: That is one of the things: there is less of a revelation of G-dliness. You see renewal most in people, then animals, then plants, least in inanimate things, where the vessel dominates and the light shows least. Still, look into the rock and you see it, without going to the molecular level. Rocks are like fruits of trees: mountains and the earth make diamonds, and the world keeps renewing its elements as they are used up, washed away and corroded. Watch a nature show: rivers carve huge valleys, the wind erodes, even the hardest rock changes, "it's like the living planet." Fast-forward films of one place over a month show it eaten away and rebuilt into new rock, only much more slowly.

blocks.text: In between is the light of *Atzilus* that comes out of *Adam Kadmon*. There is the expression through vessels, limited ways, which we appreciate most; there is G-d's choice to reveal Himself through it; and in between is this light: the thing inherently exists in everything. Since G-d is infinite and not for any reason, once He connected Himself to *chesed*, to creating, everything is inherently created by Him in an infinite way, as the nature of things, not limited to particular instances or circumstances.

blocks.text: In the vessel of *chesed* it is revealed at certain times and not others; some things you see as creation, some not. In the light of *chesed* of *Atzilus* it is infinite, axiomatic: everything must be recreated every moment by G-d. That comes from the *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon*, where G-d associated Himself with this *midda* (attribute) and gave it His properties. Then He chose the vessel of *chesed* of *Atzilus* to show it more openly in certain things, so it would not be like *Tohu* (the world of Chaos), where all the *middos* are equally infinite all the time and none can be appreciated over another.

Yet any one of them could explain every aspect of the tree, since each extends to everything: "You don't have to call the wisdom wisdom, you could call it *chesed*."

blocks.text: All the amazing detail of the tree need not be G-d's wisdom; it can be G-d's creation, creating in all these ways: the system, the way the tree works, the wisdom itself, that it seems graceful and beautiful to you, all of it created. That is *Tohu*, where all are infinite and equal. When they went into the vessels, we came to see aspects of G-dliness individually, in different things, which lets us focus on some and appreciate them more and less.

blocks.title: A walk in the woods
blocks.text:
Now we see only one at a time, in a limited way, sometimes more and sometimes less. When Rabbi Walters walks through the woods here, he sees G-dliness more easily than sitting in his house or the synagogue: the wisdom and beauty of nature, more life and vitality, than plasterboard walls that are man-made. To him that covers up the G-dliness: he does not see G-d's direct involvement, because it went through so many intermediaries of man. Man only manipulates what G-d made, and his intellect and abilities are from G-d, so G-d made the house too, but he does not see it as much.

In a way G-d's wisdom is even more expressed in the house: it is not direct, so G-d has to pull all these strings, arranging things to influence the architects so it comes out this way.

blocks.text: He once heard that you are not supposed to contemplate man-made things for the greatness of the Creator. He thinks it is different if you turn it into a G-d-made thing: the point is not to marvel at how big a skyscraper is and conclude that G-d is even greater, since that is being impressed by human achievement. He never saw the source and cannot really say, but there is probably something to it. "You can make an *inyan* on everything, for sure."

blocks.text: On the other hand, he really likes going out to nature. In a city, man has covered over G-dliness with cement and wood and whatever, and *mamash* makes a *kelipa* (lit. husk; what conceals G-dliness) that makes it harder to see: they cover it up with all their stuff.

blocks.text: That is like *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon* and *chachma* of *Atzilus*: the wisdom in the tree, and its coming in a specific form, what we know as wisdom and order. People do not realize that G-d created the whole idea of order, that certain things strike us as graceful, logical and beautiful, as having a design. Nowadays people are starting to appreciate that chaos itself has an order, the whole chaos theory, and a beauty, and to blur the line between order and chaos, seeing that each has both in it; that paradox is in a way its greatest beauty.

blocks.text: This deeper view stems from G-d creating the very idea of what is logical, beautiful and graceful. So inherently it is not an order but really a chaos: G-d chooses to do whatever He wants, and He chose to make it logical. Why should a certain thing be logical? We see one and one making two as obviously so only because G-d made us that way. "It'd be a whole different reality if G-d made different *kelim* in *Atzilus*."

blocks.text: That is why the lights of *Atzilus* are still called the ten *sefiros b'li ma*. Compared to *Adam Kadmon* they are already very tangible: in them, before the vessel, G-d is revealed as infinitely wise, as essentially a creator, so everything is created by Him every moment, every aspect of it. Seemingly that is very limited from *Adam Kadmon*'s point of view, where G-d was higher than creation and chose to connect Himself to it. Now you define G-d by that quality.

blocks.text: Still, it is *b'li ma* compared to the vessels of *Atzilus*. That G-d is inherently a creator is infinite and undefined compared to the particular creations that will manifest it. It can be infinite because G-d connected it to His essence: as He is infinite, unlimited, with free choice, so this quality is infinite, bound to nothing, able to come out any way He chooses. Though it is just a color, not essentially connected to His essence, once He connected Himself to it, it becomes intrinsic and takes on the qualities of His essence by association.

blocks.question: How do we see it in a tree?
blocks.text:
The tree is only one example of the way a tree could be. G-d could use the same creative ability, the same wisdom, to make it in infinite ways. We see the inherent ability behind it, and that this tree is one representation of it. So many trees, each one different, always growing new things: that diversity shows more and more that it is infinite. It is a creative ability, and G-d chooses how it comes out; it is not a system, a machine pumping things out in strict order. It has an element of chaos and free choice.

But an example within the tree already shows how it is revealed in the vessels, with the light behind it. The light itself is the concept, which is what he said first.

blocks.text: That everything must be recreated every moment by G-d, as the way reality is, is the real light of *chesed* of *Atzilus*. Seeing it in a tree is that light manifest through the vessel of *Atzilus* into *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*: a glimmer of a glimmer of a glimmer. Still it is important to see it there, in a *prat*, because in the *pratim* it becomes close to you. Then you extrapolate the *klal*: not just a tree, but that the nature of reality is to depend on G-d every moment to be recreated.

blocks.text: The *hisbonenus* (contemplation): how do I see that in a tree, in a bug, in the stock market? When you can point to how each reflects the truth, it becomes much more apparent and real to you. The *pratim* are only a reflection, enclothed in the *kelim* and the *osios* of thought, speech and action, down to *Asiya*, a glimmer of a glimmer of a glimmer, yet in the *prat* you see the *klal* more truly. So you need both: first recognize the *klal*, as we are doing now, then contemplate the *pratim* and see it in the tree.
